I am an Economist and Data Scientist in the Pricing Algorithms team at Wayfair, where I use causal inference, machine learning and applied econometrics to optimize pricing. Before that, I was an Associate Professor of Applied Economics at Johns Hopkins University (Carey Business School), where I studied how social and strategic interactions shape individual and aggregate outcomes, using economic theory, econometrics, ML, applied probability and computational methods. Affiliations included the Hopkins Population Center, Institute for Data Intensive Engineering and Science (DIES), and the Data Science and AI Institute. My academic research is published in top economics journals, such as Econometrica, Review of Economics and Statistics, Journal of Business and Economic Statistics, American Economic Journal, ACM EC, and others.

title: Research
text:
Selected papers

A Strategic Model of Software Dependency Networks
Cornelius Fritz, Co-Pierre Georg, Angelo Mele, Michael Schweinberger · ACM EC24, 2024
Structural model of dependency networks among software packages; externalities, competition, homophily.
PDF


Spectral estimation of large stochastic blockmodels with discrete nodal covariates
Lingxin Hao, Joshua Cape, Angelo Mele, Carey Priebe · JBES 41(4), 2023
ASE for SBMs with discrete covariates; scales well; CLT for covariate parameters.
PDF · Code (grdpg)


A model of inter-organizational network formation
Shweta Gaonkar, Angelo Mele · Journal of Economic Behavior and Organization 214, 2023
Network formation with application to VC co-investment; entry and capital requirements counterfactuals.
PDF · Code/Data


Approximate Variational Estimation for a Model of Network Formation
Lingjiong Zhu, Angelo Mele · Review of Economics and Statistics 105(1), 2023
Mean-field variational approximation of ERGM normalizing constant; iterative \(n^2\) algorithm.
PDF · Code (mfergm)


A structural model of dense network formation
Econometrica 85(3), 2017
Structural model of dense network formation.
PDF · Published · Code (netnew)
